sentence: The minutes should leave open how many members agreed, while making clear that agreement was not unanimous.
setupText: Choose the sentence that rules out complete agreement but does not rule out some agreement.
taskText: The minutes should leave open how many members agreed, while making clear that agreement was not unanimous.
text: Choose the sentence that rules out complete agreement but does not rule out some agreement. The minutes should leave open how many members agreed, while making clear that agreement was not unanimous.
explanation: Not every denies agreement by the entire group while leaving possible agreement by some members.

This says all members opposed the proposal, a stronger claim than lack of unanimity.
Not every denies agreement by the entire group while leaving possible agreement by some members.
No member excludes any agreement, which the requested wording must leave possible.
This asserts the unanimity that the minutes must rule out.

sentence: Only some of the applications were approved.
setupText: Choose the conclusion guaranteed by the wording.
taskText: Only some of the applications were approved.
text: Choose the conclusion guaranteed by the wording. Only some of the applications were approved.
options: Fewer than half of the applications were approved.
At least one application was approved and at least one was not.
Exactly half of the applications were approved.
One application was approved and the rest were rejected.
answer: At least one application was approved and at least one was not.
explanation: 'Only some' indicates a nonempty approved subset smaller than the whole group.

rationales.Fewer than half of the applications were: Only some excludes all, but it does not specify whether approval was below half.
rationales.Exactly half of the applications were ap: No exact fraction is given; some could cover different-sized subsets.
rationales.At least one application was approved an: 'Only some' indicates a nonempty approved subset smaller than the whole group.
rationales.One application was approved and the res: The wording does not give an exact number or say that nonapproved applications were rejected rather than pending.

taskText: We used ___ to check the figures before the meeting began.
text: Choose the phrase meaning all the small amount of time available. We used ___ to check the figures before the meeting began.
focusKey: coverage-determiners-and-quantifiers-b2-1143:What little as a total limited quantity
explanation: What little time we had combines the smallness of the supply with using all of it.

rationales.the little time we needed: This describes the small amount required, not all the time actually available.
rationales.as little time as possible: This means minimizing time spent, rather than using the entire limited supply.
rationales.a little more time: This refers to an additional small amount, not the whole existing allowance.
rationales.what little time we had: What little time we had combines the smallness of the supply with using all of it.

sentence: All employees who handle customer payments must attend the briefing.
setupText: Choose the group that the sentence requires to attend. Do not add people outside its wording.
taskText: All employees who handle customer payments must attend the briefing.
text: Choose the group that the sentence requires to attend. Do not add people outside its wording. All employees who handle customer payments must attend the briefing.
options: Every employee whose work includes handling customer payments.
Every employee, whatever their duties involve.
Some employees selected from those who handle payments.
Every employee who handles any customer information.
answer: Every employee whose work includes handling customer payments.
explanation: Who handle customer payments restricts the group; all includes every employee within that group.

rationales.Every employee whose work includes handl: Who handle customer payments restricts the group; all includes every employee within that group.
rationales.Every employee, whatever their duties in: The relative clause limits the group to employees handling payments.
rationales.Some employees selected from those who h: All includes the whole payment-handling group, not a selected portion.
rationales.Every employee who handles any customer: Customer information is broader than customer payments and changes the stated group.

sentence: The committee considered two proposals and rejected both of them.
setupText: Choose the conclusion that follows from the committee's decision.
taskText: The committee considered two proposals and rejected both of them.
text: Choose the conclusion that follows from the committee's decision. The committee considered two proposals and rejected both of them.
options: One proposal was rejected; the other was accepted.
focusKey: coverage-determiners-and-quantifiers-b2-1145:Both rejected versus partial and complete negation
explanation: Rejection of both proposals means acceptance of neither; 'neither' applies separately to the two members.

Not both denies rejection of the complete pair, but the committee rejected the pair.
Rejection of both proposals means acceptance of neither; 'neither' applies separately to the two members.
This excludes rejection of either proposal, reversing the decision.
rationales.One proposal was rejected; the other was: This splits the outcomes between the two proposals, whereas both had the same rejection outcome.

sentence: A technician visits the site every few days.
setupText: Choose the interpretation that preserves the approximate frequency.
taskText: A technician visits the site every few days.
text: Choose the interpretation that preserves the approximate frequency. A technician visits the site every few days.
options: Exactly three days separate every pair of visits.
The technician makes several visits during each day.
There are a few visits in total and then they stop.
Visits recur after short intervals of several days.
answer: Visits recur after short intervals of several days.
focusKey: coverage-determiners-and-quantifiers-b2-1146:Every few plus a plural time unit
explanation: 'Every few days' describes repeated visits at short, nonexact multi-day intervals.

rationales.Exactly three days separate every pair o: A few does not fix an exact three-day interval.
rationales.The technician makes several visits duri: Every few days measures the interval between visits, not visits per day.
rationales.Visits recur after short intervals of se: 'Every few days' describes repeated visits at short, nonexact multi-day intervals.
rationales.There are a few visits in total and then: The phrase describes a recurring schedule, not the total number of visits.

explanation: The formal expression 'many a' takes a singular noun and verb while referring to many individuals.

rationales.Many of the residents: This plural subject also requires have raised.
rationales.Many resident: 'Many' directly before a count noun requires plural 'residents'; alternatively use 'many a resident'.
rationales.Many a resident: The formal expression 'many a' takes a singular noun and verb while referring to many individuals.

rationales.enough: Enough states that the support met a need, which the task does not authorize.
rationales.a little: A little presents a small amount, not the substantial amount requested.
rationales.a good deal: The expression needs 'of' before the noun phrase 'public support'.

sentence: I contacted ___ former managers for references.
setupText: Choose the phrase that makes a grammatical sentence.
taskText: I contacted ___ former managers for references.
text: Choose the phrase that makes a grammatical sentence. I contacted ___ former managers for references.
focusKey: coverage-determiners-and-quantifiers-b2-1149:Ordering all, a number and a possessive
explanation: All three of my identifies and includes the full group of three former managers.

rationales.all of three my: The number and possessive are misplaced; use 'all three of my former managers'.
rationales.all three of my: All three of my identifies and includes the full group of three former managers.
rationales.my all three: All normally precedes the possessive in this pattern: all my three or all three of my.
rationales.all three of the my: 'The' and 'my' cannot both occupy the determiner position before 'former managers'.

sentence: Neither of the two routes avoids the toll bridge.
setupText: Choose the statement equivalent to the original.
taskText: Neither of the two routes avoids the toll bridge.
text: Choose the statement equivalent to the original. Neither of the two routes avoids the toll bridge.
options: Both routes avoid the toll bridge.
One route uses the toll bridge and one avoids it.
Both routes use the toll bridge.
At least one route avoids the toll bridge.
answer: Both routes use the toll bridge.
explanation: If neither route avoids the bridge, each of the two routes goes via it.

This reverses the negative claim: neither route avoids it.
rationales.One route uses the toll bridge and one a: Neither excludes an avoiding route among the two.
If neither route avoids the bridge, each of the two routes goes via it.
rationales.At least one route avoids the toll bridg: This asserts an exception that neither explicitly rules out.

sentence: Contact the supplier if you notice ___.

taskText: Contact the supplier if you notice ___.
text: Choose the phrase that requires reporting even one additional fault, without setting a minimum above one. Contact the supplier if you notice ___.
explanation: Any in this condition covers even one new fault without requiring a specified number.

rationales.several further faults: Several sets a higher trigger than a single further fault.
rationales.many further faults: Many waits for a large number, contrary to reporting even one.
rationales.both further faults: Both presupposes a known pair of additional faults and includes the pair.
rationales.any further faults: Any in this condition covers even one new fault without requiring a specified number.

focusKey: coverage-determiners-and-quantifiers-b2-1152:The other plus a number for a complete remainder
explanation: The other seven identifies all seven files remaining after three of ten are accounted for.

rationales.the other seven: The other seven identifies all seven files remaining after three of ten are accounted for.
rationales.another seven: Another seven introduces an additional quantity without explicitly identifying the remainder of this set.
rationales.seven others: 'Seven others' refers to seven different files but does not explicitly mark them as the entire known remainder.
rationales.other seven: 'Other seven' lacks the determiner needed to identify these seven remaining files.

my monthly salary and a half
explanation: 'Half' can directly precede a possessive noun phrase; half of 2,000 is 1,000.

rationales.my monthly salary and a half: A salary and a half totals 3,000 euros, more than the entire salary.

sentence: Of the 90 survey respondents, 60 preferred evening classes. ___ preferred evening classes.

explanation: Sixty out of ninety is two-thirds; of connects the fraction to the identified group.

rationales.Half of the respondents: Half of ninety is forty-five, not the sixty who preferred evening classes.
rationales.Two-thirds of the respondents: Sixty out of ninety is two-thirds; of connects the fraction to the identified group.

explanation: The number of complaints makes the count the singular subject, so has risen is appropriate.

rationales.A number of: 'A number of complaints' means several complaints and normally takes a plural verb, 'have'.
rationales.The number of: The number of complaints makes the count the singular subject, so has risen is appropriate.

rationales.no less than: No less than emphasizes that the amount reached 40,000 euros and presents that amount as strikingly large.

sentence: A row of lamps runs along either side of the footbridge.

rationales.There is a row of lamps on each of the t: In this descriptive use, 'either side' means each of the two sides, so lamps line both sides.
rationales.There is a row on one side, but the sent: That treats 'either' as an unspecified choice; the task asks for its normal distributive reading here.
